titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 50: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 50. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The restoration [........ ⲟⲩⲛ] holds eight dots (817–1002) followed by restored letters.

The framed manuscript page number [ⲛ] (top left) is printed in restoration brackets with a bar above and below as the frame; the running title [ⲛⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ] is restored, with a stroke over ⲛ. Stroke over the restored ⲛ of ⲟⲩⲛ (1060–1072). Reconcile flags on this page are explained by dots of area < 6 (ll. 1, 5, 6, 7, 9, 17 ⲁϥ ..., 18 ⲑ, 31, 33) and by dot rows at the zone centre (ll. 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 32), which it does not count; every dot was counted on the 4× sheets, and ll. 11 and 14 were checked blob by blob.
Dot under ⲙ of ⲙⲛ (949). Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲁⲩ (1203–1215).

Nomen-sacrum bar over ⲏⲥ of ⲓⲏⲥ (907–933, pixel rows 394–395): ⲏ 100 %, ⲥ 100 %, ⲓ 0 %; diaeresis over ⲓ (897/902). Strokes over the restored ⲣ of ⲡⲡ[ⲣⲓⲉ] (1005–1017) and ⲛ of ϩⲛ (1087–1099). Dots under ⲉ and ⲓ (at its foot) of ⲧⲉϥϭⲓⲛⲉⲓ (1216, 1227). The strokes tool also reports the descender of ϩ of l. 2 (826–834).
